messages:
ana: quick heads-up — ran a focused profile on reranker-nonchat after yesterday's change. seeing p95 regressions at higher QPS, attaching notes and configs below.

mike: can you share numbers? QPS / batch sizes?

ana: QPS ~250 sustained during the run. avg batch size ~18 by count but token-weighted average is spiky because a few requests set high token budgets (some max_tokens=1024 from experiments). p50 ~ 72ms, p95 jumped to ~210ms at peak.

jess: is this specific to the token_weighted batcher change or kernel selection?

ana: looks like both. profiling shows frequent kernel fallback for small/irregular GEMM shapes and KV cache churn. flamegraph: https://internal-graphs/reports/1805557777/flame (paste). GC spikes line up with big-batch formation.

sylvia: wait — reranker non-chat shouldn't be using KV cache much. where's the churn coming from?

ana: some requests reuse prefixes for multi-call scoring which accidentally hits the kvcache. after token_budget_estimate tweak, we let huge budgets into batches which increases memory working set and causes more evictions.

mike: do you have the batcher config used?

ana: snippet:
```
batcher:
  mode: token_weighted
  token_cap_per_batch: 12000
  per_request_token_limit: 1024
  queue_timeout_ms: 60
  fairness: time_bias
```

kai: time_bias fairness prioritizes older requests which is fine, but combined with high per_request_token_limit it lets big requests dominate a batch. that explains batch skew.

jess: proposed fix: enforce a per-request contribution cap when forming a token-weighted batch. e.g. contribution = min(request_tokens, 256). That limits domination by large budgets. also reduce queue_timeout to 40ms to favor small, low-token requests.

mike: and on kernel side? we saw fallback to a slower GEMM path for shapes < 128 sometimes. can we add a kernel-hint for those shapes on reranker?

kai: yes — runtime flag available: `kernel.force_hint=fast_gemm_small`. we can scope it to the reranker-nonchat route. it biases kernel selection without changing model weights. test first in canary.

ana: experiment plan: create two toggles — (1) `exp/emb-batch-cap-256` to enforce per-request cap + queue_timeout=40ms, (2) `exp/kernel-hint-small-fast` to apply kernel hint. rollout 10% traffic for 2 hours during US peak. measure p50/p95, tokens/sec, batch size distribution, kvcache evictions, and a new metric `batch_domination_ratio` (percent of batches where top-3 requests >50% tokens).

sylvia: add an eval check for reranker scoring since kernel changes sometimes slightly shift FP behavior: `eval.check=rerkank-small-q` (small eval set). fail rollout if MRR drops >0.5 pt.

mike: I can wire dashboards and an alert: if p95 > 150ms or batch_domination_ratio > 10% revert automatically.

runtime-bot: deploy job #4021 started: exp/emb-batch-cap-256 -> reranker-nonchat (10%). CI passed.

ana: quick note — observed potential quality drift in a separate run when forcing a different fast kernel on quantized path. adding the eval guard above.

jess: after the 2h window, can we collect: median batch size, p95, KV evictions delta, tokens/sec, and distribution of per-request token contributions?

ana: yes — I'll collect and post. early dry-run shows batch_domination_ratio down from 24% -> 4% with the cap, p95 dropped from ~210ms -> 95ms. KV evictions down ~40%.

sylvia: promising. any effect on quality so far?

ana: no measurable MRR change on the small eval set for this run. will run full eval overnight.

kai: if stable, recommend defaults: token_cap_per_batch -> 8000, per_request_contribution_cap -> 256, queue_timeout_ms -> 50, kernel hint off-by-default with opt-in for rerankers.

mike: pragmatic rollback order: kernel-hint -> batcher-config. kernel hint is lower risk to revert quickly.

ana: thanks all — running full eval now. will attach result graphs here when ready.

ana: (final) experiment ended: 2h run, 10% traffic. results: p95 210ms -> 95ms, p50 steady at ~70ms, batch_domination_ratio 24%->3.8%, KV evictions -42%, tokens/sec +12%. full eval MRR change = -0.03 pt (within noise). rolling to 50% and scheduling canary for global rollout.
